008163281501b0ea: KUALA LUMPUR: The Badminton Association of Malaysia will look into tapping the RM30 million sports matching grant scheme announced in the 2027 budget to strengthen tournament organisation and provide more exposure for back-up players, BAM president Tengku Zafrul Aziz said.
He said the grant initiative would create a competitive platform domestically, allowing local players to gain experience before progressing to the international stage.

“For badminton, more quality tournaments mean more opportunities for local players to test their abilities, face stronger opponents and gain experience before competing on the international stage,” he said in a statement today.

He said such competitive exposure was important to overcome the reliance on a handful of established star players and to build a system for grooming the next generation. “Our challenge is to ensure that when a champion retires, there are already back-up players ready to take their place. This requires consistent talent development, quality coaching and comprehensive sports science support,” he said.
Tengku Zafrul said BAM's focus was not merely on achieving immediate success, but also on ensuring that Malaysian badminton remained competitive for generations to come.

On developing young athletes, he said the increase in sports funding at school level was a positive step, but a strong development pathway was needed to ensure that identified talent did not fall by the wayside.
At the same time, the national badminton squad's preparations for the 2027 SEA Games remained a priority.
The 2027 federal budget estimates tabled yesterday provides RM460 million for national sports development and RM240 million for preparations to host the 2027 SEA Games and Asean Para Games.
9cb2f8f55e5e84b9: RIYADH: Yemen's Houthis attacked Riyadh's international airport with a missile on Saturday, a diplomatic source told AFP, with dozens reported wounded and a witness describing panic in the terminal.

Saudi authorities did not confirm any new attack or evacuation, but one witness reported hearing an explosion while waiting to board a flight, and another said they saw a strike that left people wounded.
"I was on gate 403" at the domestic terminal, the witness told AFP.
"I saw 401 hit, I saw injured in front of my eyes. Everyone was running."
A source at a local hospital told AFP that five people were in intensive care after being wounded at the airport, saying "dozens of people were injured" in all.
The relative of one injured person said they had been wounded in the shoulders and arms by shattered glass, and had been taken to hospital.
Three witnesses confirmed people being evacuated from the airport.
"Houthis are attacking civilian targets. Riyadh airport is a civilian target," the diplomatic source told AFP, saying the airport was hit by "a missile around 3:00 pm" (1200 GMT).
The airport was hit by deadly attacks claimed by Yemen's Houthis on Thursday, though the Iran-backed group did not announce any fresh strikes on the facility on Saturday.
The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen's Riyadh-backed government unravelled in July.
Admissions by Saudi authorities of strikes hitting civilian targets are relatively rare, with officials issuing few statements on Houthi attacks in recent weeks.
The scale and frequency of the recent strikes targeting Riyadh are unprecedented in the eight months of war that has spread across the Middle East.
Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that supports Yemen's government militarily, and has found itself drawn deeper into its impoverished neighbour's civil war.
Both Riyadh and the Houthis have signalling a willingness to keep fighting rather than pursue diplomacy.

Earlier on Saturday, Riyadh airport urged passengers to check their flight status before coming -- echoing an advisory sent on Thursday, when attacks killed three people including a pilot for Saudia, the national airline.
"Please contact your airline directly and confirm your flight status before heading to the airport," read a statement posted on the airport's official X account on Saturday.
Thursday's Houthi-claimed attacks also badly damaged a grounded Saudia plane.
Meanwhile, in Yemen, Saudi-supported government forces were advancing against the Houthis in areas they captured last month around the Bab al-Mandab strait, military sources told AFP.
The Yemeni government last week announced a counter-offensive aimed at retaking all areas held by the Houthis, after the group seized the country's entire western coastline in a lightning offensive.
The Houthis confirmed that government forces had attacked in the Bab al-Mandab area -- a key chokepoint for Red Sea oil and cargo shipping -- but they claimed to have repelled the assault.
Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.
bd4015c0ecc00830: INITIATIVES to label books as written by humans, and not artificial intelligence (AI), are gaining ground following a string of scandals where authors were suspected of using the technology without admitting it.

Several labelling schemes, including from Britain, France and Germany, were being showcased at the world's biggest book industry fair in Frankfurt this week, where the challenges posed by AI were hotly debated.

Among recent cases where authors allegedly used AI, the most high-profile is that of Haitian-Canadian author Thelyson Orelien, which has rocked the French-language literary world. He has denied the claims.
The affair was a "real earthquake" for the French book trade, said Charlotte Allibert, co-founder of Librinova, a self-publishing company and literary agency.
The French group runs a scheme under which authors can get their books assessed and then labelled as a "human creation" for a small fee, with about 200 works given the stamp.
Writers who want the label have their works run through AI detection software and undergo an interview with an auditor, who also checks the book personally.
"It's reassuring for authors to know that we're committed to this issue," said Allibert.
"More and more, authors are afraid of being suspected of using AI. Self-published authors even more so."
Another scheme is from British startup Books by People, which this week announced its certification mark for human-authored works had been registered by the intellectual property office.

To get the stamp, titles have to meet the group's "organic literature" standards, which require the writing to originate from its author while allowing limited use of AI for tasks such as spelling or grammar checks.
Publishers sign up to the scheme for a fee and can then request to get their authors' books labelled with the Books by People mark.
The scheme launched with five independent publishers and is set to announce more members in the coming months.
In the United States, writers group the Authors Guild has introduced a "human authored" certification mark.
It is a self-certification system that requires authors to sign a licence agreement. Around 6,500 titles have received the stamp.

The controversy surrounding Orelien erupted last month when an anonymous X account alleged the 38-year-old used AI to write his debut novel, It Was Either That or Die, based on analysis of excerpts by AI-detection websites.
He has denied the claims and believes the attacks on his work are racially motivated, although the scandal led to him being dropped from France's top literary prize.
There have also been a string of other cases in recent times.
Earlier this year, publisher Hachette cancelled the release of horror novel Shy Girl by Mia Ballard in the US and withdrew the book from sale in Britain over allegations of AI use.
In comments to the New York Times, Ballard denied using AI, but said that an acquaintance she hired to edit the book, which was originally self-published, had used AI.
Despite the mounting scandals, some in the book trade view the idea of labels with scepticism.
Current schemes mostly allow a minimal use of AI, for example for research and grammar checks, but there are worries this could be open to interpretation.
There are also concerns it could be too easy to circumvent checks in the fledgling initiatives and pass off AI-produced books as human-written.
Sebastian Guggolz, head of the German Publishers and Booksellers Association, said the book trade was struggling with what approach to take.
"There's no simple 'with AI' or 'without AI'," he said at the book fair.
"The question has to go deeper. It has to be addressed to each individual and to the entire industry: how do we want to make our practices transparent?"
* The writer is from AFP

5b92e6e32da8c203: THE United States has announced sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) that threaten to cripple its operations and spark fresh transatlantic tension.
Washington's unprecedented move was an "assault on the rule of law", said the ICC.
Based in the Dutch city of The Hague, the ICC tries individuals suspected of the world's worst offences — war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide.
Established in 2002 by the Rome Statute, it currently has 125 members. Major powers, such as the US, Russia, China and India, as well as Israel, are not members of the court.
It is governed by a strict policy of "complementarity", meaning it can take on cases only a suspect's home country is unwilling or unable to try itself.
Since its establishment, the court has convicted 15 people, with four acquitted.
Critics say the court has focused too heavily on war crimes committed in Africa and failed to convict major political leaders.
However, its most high-profile current case concerns ex-Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte, the first former Asian head of state to stand in the ICC dock.
The court employs around 900 employees from 100 nationalities. It is often confused with the International Court of Justice, also based in The Hague, which settles disputes between countries.
US President Donald Trump's administration has issued several rounds of sanctions against top ICC officials, but these latest announced actions go further, targeting the entire court.
ICC officials are concerned about access to banking, credit card facilities, insurance and especially technology, given a heavy reliance on US systems.

Acting chief prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang said: "We are trying to find alternative means, maybe not as effective as the US technology, but at least to be able to maintain our independence, to be able to continue to work."
The prosecutor, himself the target of sanctions, said they crippled daily life — he was unable to book transport, hotels or conduct banking operations.
But expanding them to the entire institution raises questions about the ICC's ability to pay staff, conduct investigations abroad, protect witnesses and even operate its detention facilities.
"This is a test of our resilience," said Niang.
As the host city, the Dutch have a special responsibility to the ICC under the terms of a "Headquarters Agreement" signed in 2008.
This obliges the Netherlands to protect ICC facilities and staff, provide "any means of communication" and ensure "freedom of financial assets from restrictions".
In an unusually fiery speech last month at the United Nations General Assembly, Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten vowed to defend the ICC "in my country, in my city".
"How can you possibly be opposed to prosecuting the very worst crimes?
"I believe there can be only one response: 'hands off the ICC'," said Jetten to warm applause.
Reacting to the announcement from Washington, Jetten said the Dutch would do "whatever we need" to ensure the ICC could continue to function.
One possibility would be for the European Commission to deploy a legal instrument known as the "blocking mechanism".
This prohibits European firms from obeying the US sanctions "actively or by deliberate omission", giving the European Union a potential means of cushioning some of the impact.
The EU blocking mechanism is seen as the "nuclear option", said Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen, adding that the Netherlands had nevertheless asked Brussels to prepare it.
Jetten said a six-month pause before sanctions took effect should be used to pursue dialogue with Washington.

The US is furious the court issued an arrest warrant for close ally Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over alleged crimes in Gaza. It is also concerned an ICC investigation into Afghanistan could result in accusations against US personnel.
Trump has upped his rhetoric against what he called a "rogue institution" and "evil group of people" and the US has vowed to dismantle the court "brick-by-brick".
But even under less pugnacious presidents, Washington has never been a fan of the ICC and never considered joining.
The US has a law dubbed the "Hague Invasion Act", allowing it to take "all means necessary and appropriate" to defend US personnel or allies detained by the ICC.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
e93ffcdb4f857f7b: LONDON: Several thousand pro-Palestinian protesters marched through central London on Saturday, calling for an end to Israeli strikes on Gaza, three years after Hamas' Oct 7 attack.
Marchers carried placards reading "End the genocide" and "Free Palestine" as they made their way along the route near the British parliament.
"We are here today to mark three years of the ongoing genocide in Gaza," Aimee Shalan, director of the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, told AFP.
She said UK-led Western sanctions over settler violence did not go far enough, calling for "full sanctions on Israel".
A ceasefire began a year ago and although Israel has reduced its level of attacks it has kept striking Gaza on a near-daily basis.
Strikes have killed some 1,450 Palestinians since the ceasefire, according to Gaza's health ministry.
Recent graduate Hibo Hassan, 23, said he wanted to show his solidarity.
"Although it is happening in the Middle East, it affects us here now," he said.
"It's extremely dystopian and that is something we should be all scared about," he added.
The "National March for Palestine" organised by the Palestine Coalition, according to police, came three days after the third anniversary of the Oct 7, 2023 attack.
The attack was the deadliest in Israel's history, resulting in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.
Militants also dragged 251 hostages into Gaza, 44 of them already dead.
In response, Israel launched a military offensive that has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gaza's health ministry.
A small counter-demonstration was organised by Stop The Hate UK, a Jewish-led, pro-Israel campaign group.

Ahead of the march, London's Metropolitan police said it would be using powers under public order legislation to require anyone wearing a face covering to deliberately hide their identity to remove it.
"We will take a zero-tolerance approach to hate crime and other offending," said senior Met officer Carl Galvin.

5d1899bd81014574: OSLO: The winner of this year's Nobel Peace Prize, judge and former UN rights chief Navi Pillay, on Saturday called sanctions announced by the US on the International Criminal Court (ICC) "unheard of, unacceptable".

"There is so much tension and anxiety over the continued existence of international courts, mainly the International Criminal Court in The Hague," Pillay said via video link from Nuremberg during an event at the Nobel Peace Center in Oslo.
Pillay also lamented that "there are hundreds of staff who feel they are under threat".

"Most importantly, sanctions have been announced by one country against the judges, just for the judicial orders they issue. This is unheard of, unacceptable," the 85-year-old South African lawyer said.
The Norwegian Nobel Committee on Friday announced that Pillay, who once sat on the ICC, was this year's recipient of the prestigious Nobel Peace Prize.
Both the US, whose leader Donald Trump has long coveted the award for himself, and ally Israel condemned her being awarded the honour.
Hours after Pillay was named the laureate, the US announced new sanctions against the ICC, provoking swift condemnation from member states and the UN.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington would ban transactions with what he described as a "rogue court", escalating a long-running campaign by Trump's administration against the Hague-based tribunal.
The court rejected the US sanctions as an attack on international law and warned in a statement that "history will judge this moment".

In addition to serving on the ICC, Pillay was the UN human rights high commissioner from 2008 to 2014 and she headed the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry (COI), which found last year that genocide was occurring in Gaza. The body does not speak on behalf of the UN.
Israel has rejected the COI's findings, calling them "distorted and false".
Israel's foreign ministry said the award legitimised "anti-Israel hatred", adding that it thought that Nazi propagandist Joseph Goebbels must be "applauding from hell".
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the awarding of the prize to Pillay showed the Nobel committee had "lost its moral compass" by honouring "a bigot".

Trump, who last month called on ICC member states to quit the court, meanwhile labelled the committee's choice as "a disgraceful and embarrassing decision", telling a rally of his supporters in Syracuse, New York he had "never heard of" Pillay.

2bb7b1eea63f3018: PETALING JAYA: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim tonight admitted that all the country’s economic woes would not be resolved by the 2027 budget estimates tabled yesterday.
However, he said the government will focus on cushioning the impact of rising prices of goods and certain services on the public.
Savings made from curbing leakages and better governance will be redirected to the people, Anwar said in a special interview on the budget broadcast today, Bernama reported.
He cited the increase in cost of imported phosphate fertiliser due to the closure of the Hormuz Strait in the wake of the US-led war against Iran, as an example.

Anwar said while fluctuations in commodity prices, logistics costs, and disruptions in international supply chains were beyond the government’s control, Putrajaya could help reduce the financial pressure.
One such way is by streamlining the supply chain, expanding farmers’ markets, and increasing sales of goods through the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority, he said.

Anwar said a stronger fiscal position could be achieved via more disciplined financial management, enabling the government to provide assistance such as sports shoes for schoolchildren, as well as allowances and minimum income support for rubber smallholders and paddy farmers.
“This can all be achieved if we manage finances well and ensure that government expenditure truly reaches the targeted groups,” he was quoted as saying.
Anwar also said initiatives outlined in the 2027 budget were aimed at ensuring a better quality of life for the people, while taking into account the challenges the public endured.
“The economy may be thriving, but the people may still be burdened. We take a more holistic approach and that is essentially what a budget is (about).”
He said the 2027 budget not only focussed on significant matters such as spurring economic growth, but also extended to issues such as the welfare of gig workers, welfare of pets and minimum wage.
The federal budget estimates provide for a total expenditure of RM460 billion, an increase of RM40 billion from the 2026 estimates.

2fade94490d8894e: SAN FRANCISCO: An artificial intelligence model developed by Anthropic submitted a fabricated tip about an unsolved homicide to Philadelphia police, authorities said Friday, criticising the company for taking two months to report the incident.
The Philadelphia Police Department said the false submission was made in July through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, a public website where people can share information about unsolved killings.

According to Anthropic's account, as relayed by police, the model was running a test that involved interacting with randomly selected websites when it reached the site and filed false information about an unsolved murder.
The AI model presented itself as someone who might have knowledge of the case.

The incident echoed other recent cases of unintended behavior involving AI models, including one where an OpenAI agent undergoing a security evaluation broke out of its testing environment and breached systems at AI platform Hugging Face.
Anthropic's breaches have prompted the White House to mandate that AI companies notify and correct security incidents, news outlet Axios reported citing administration officials.
"This notification and remediation process is not optional... It is a critical national security obligation," White House Super Intelligence Force leaders said in a statement to Axios.
The episode heightened concerns about the industry's increased use of AI agents, systems programmed to take multi-step actions without human supervision.
Anthropic published a report Friday outlining multiple types of "unintended" actions that its models have taken, including the incident involving the Philadelphia Police Department website.
Other organisations impacted included the White House and other US government agencies, the report said.
The newly revealed incidents "had minimal real-world impact" and were "significantly less severe" than other cybersecurity incidents previously reported, Anthropic said.
'UNACCEPTABLE' DELAY

The company outlined four categories of incidents that it found during an internal review of its Claude model: exploiting "basic" coding flaws, submitting forms on websites, bypassing requirements for tokens or fees, and using short URLs to get around other limits.

Anthropic has turned off internet access for Claude during all internal testing for now "until we have confirmed that our security and monitoring measures... reliably catch behaviors like these," the report said.
Philadelphia police said the phony tip, dated July 18, was flagged as spam and never reached the department's Real-Time Crime Centre for vetting.
They added that there was no sign that police systems had been breached or department data compromised.
Anthropic discovered the incident on September 28, shut down the automated testing process responsible and added a new validation step for future tests, police said.
The company alerted the department on October 7, and the two sides met the following day.
"The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the City is unacceptable," the department said.

Police said their safeguards had limited the impact, but that these "do not diminish the seriousness of an AI system presenting fabricated information as though it came from a person with knowledge of a homicide."
"Unsolved cases involve real victims, grieving families and investigators working to secure answers," the statement added.

2ab0dbd6b7783c35: PETALING JAYA: The Penang Hokkien dialect, the Phor Thor festival, dondang sayang, the Penang Hill railway, two temples and two cemeteries are among items which have been gazetted for preservation under the state heritage enactment.

Seven items have been declared as intangible cultural heritage. These are: the Penang Hokkien dialect, the Teong Guan Phor Thor festival, boria, ghazal parti, Penang bangsawan, silat pelaga, siku 12, and Penang dondang sayang.

In addition, seven heritage sites have been gazetted for preservation. They are: the Loo Pun Hong temple in Love Lane, which is the oldest Cantonese carpentry guild and temple in Southeast Asia; the Penang Hill funicular railway tracks and Upper Station and Lower Station; the Dato Koyah mausoleum; Thai Pak Koong Temple (Ng Suk) on King Street; the Fooi Chew Association building; and the Kwangtung and Tengchow No 1 cemetery in Mount Erskine.

State executive councillor Wong Hon Wai said today the declaration under the Penang State Heritage Enactment 2011 was part of efforts to preserve and conserve the state’s heritage for future generations to appreciate.

He said 35 intangible cultural heritage items had been declared state heritage last September, comprising 28 types of heritage food, one literary language, three cultural customs, two beliefs and one martial art. In addition, 15 heritage sites had been designated.

Chief minister Chow Kon Yeow described Penang as a unique “living museum” showcasing architecture, traditional villages, religious sites and cultural landscapes, as well as languages, food, performing arts and customs that shape the state’s character and identity.

He said today’s recognition also demonstrated that heritage conservation efforts were not limited to historic buildings and sites, but also encompassed intangible heritage that formed the soul of the community.

“We also want to add value to our heritage through festivals, heritage walks, gastronomy, digitalisation and creative economy activities, which will not only enrich the tourist experience but also create opportunities for young people, arts practitioners and local entrepreneurs,” he said.

Chow said tourism continued to show positive momentum in Penang, with almost a million international hotel guests recorded in the first quarter of this year, while 2.65 million international passenger movements took place at the airport from January to July, an increase of 11% compared with the same period last year.
Penang also recorded 285,400 medical tourists in the first half of 2026, generating RM602 million in revenue, he said.
58f188e95ae0cbd3: JOHOR BARU: All schools and educational institutions in Johor, including religious schools, will remain closed for another five days from Monday until Oct 16 due to worsening haze and unhealthy air quality.

State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made after considering prevailing air pollution conditions and in deference to the decree of Regent of Johor Tunku Ismail, who prioritises the safety, health and well-being of Johoreans, particularly students and education personnel.
He said air pollutant index (API) readings remained between 170 and 180, with no significant improvement, indicating that air quality continued to be unhealthy.
"The expected wind movement from Kalimantan between Oct 13 and 15 could bring transboundary air pollution, affecting air quality in Johor.

"The risk of rising concentrations of fine particles in the atmosphere, which could affect the respiratory system and the health of students and vulnerable groups, was also taken into account," he said in a statement today.
Naqib said stagnant atmospheric conditions and limited air movement could further hinder the dispersion of pollutants, potentially prolonging the haze.
He added that reports on the health effects of air pollution, particularly respiratory problems among children and school communities, were also considered before the decision was made.

Meanwhile, state Islamic Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said the extended closure also covered Johor Religious Schools, Johor Government Religious Secondary Schools and registered private Islamic education institutions under the Johor Islamic Religious Department (JAINJ).
He said the decision followed the state government's announcement extending the closure of educational institutions throughout Johor.
Home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) will continue during the closure, subject to the directives of the Johor State Education Department and JAINJ, respectively.
Any assessments or academic examinations affected by the closure will be rescheduled according to the arrangements set by the relevant authorities.
Both Naqib and Fared urged parents and guardians to monitor their children's health, limit outdoor activities and ensure they drink sufficient water.
They also advised parents to seek prompt medical attention if their children experience persistent coughing, sore throats, breathing difficulties or other symptoms associated with air pollution.
The state government, in collaboration with the relevant agencies, will continue monitoring API readings.

Any decision on when schools and religious institutions can resume normal operations will be announced through official channels, subject to improvements in air quality and assessments of health and safety conditions.
ff0f1963fbc4b3ec: LONDON: Arsenal roared back to beat Leeds 2-1 and pull level with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League on Saturday, hitting the ground running after the three-week international break.
Mikel Arteta's champions struggled to impose themselves against well-organised opponents in the first half but found their mojo after half-time to make it five wins from six games this season.
Defender James Justin gave Leeds a deserved lead early in the second half at the Emirates, silencing the home crowd in the October sunshine.
But Arsenal were level minutes later through Riccardo Calafiori, and substitute Bruno Guimaraes scored what turned out to be the winner after a finely crafted team goal.
The focus returned to the pitch on Saturday after the bombshell announcement that City had been found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.
But Arsenal, who had a perfect record before their 3-0 defeat by Brighton last month, struggled to break down Daniel Farke's physical team in the first half.
Noni Madueke, overlooked by Thomas Tuchel for England's most recent squad, was handed a rare start on the left of the Gunners' attack in place of the injured Christos Tzolis.
But neither he nor Bukayo Saka on the other flank had much joy against a defence that had conceded just three league goals all season.
Leeds had a couple of half-chances late in the first half.

First, Jayden Bogle and Anton Stach got in each other's way as Stach struck the ball against his teammate, and Bogle was denied from close range by Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya, who was out quickly to smother his shot.
Then Raya got down smartly to keep out a shot from Leeds defender Gabriel Gudmundsson from a tight angle.
Arsenal managed just one shot on target in the whole of the first half but the game opened up after the break, with chances at both ends.

Impressive Leeds midfielder Ao Tanaka forced Raya to tip over before Justin put his side ahead in the 55th minute, finishing sweetly from just inside the box after a Gudmundsson cross following a well-worked move down the left.
Arsenal defender Gabriel Magalhaes got a touch with his head but failed to keep the ball out of the net.
But the Gunners were back level just seven minutes later when the unmarked Calafiori finished past England international goalkeeper James Trafford after being set up by Ben White.
Worse was to come for Leeds when Guimaraes finished powerfully after some neat play down the Arsenal left, with Saka, Martin Odegaard and Declan Rice all involved.
The win takes Arsenal to 15 points, behind leaders City on goal difference.
Enzo Maresca's City, with a game in hand, are braced for a hostile reception at Liverpool on Sunday following the announcement of their guilty verdict last week.
ad61575abb14ce25: KUALA LUMPUR: Schools in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu will operate as usual tomorrow as Air Pollutant Index readings in the three states remain under control.
The states observe a Friday-Saturday weekend, making Sunday a school day.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the decision was based on the latest air quality readings.
"The Education Ministry will continue to monitor developments in air quality from time to time," she said in a statement today.
Data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System showed all monitoring stations in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu recorded readings below 100 as of 8pm today.
Kemaman recorded the highest reading in Terengganu at 89, while Sungai Petani recorded 80 in Kedah and Kota Bharu recorded 76 in Kelantan.
All readings fall within the moderate range of 51 to 100, below the unhealthy threshold of 101.
On Oct 8, Fadhlina announced the closure of all schools in Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as schools in Rompin, Pahang, following the worsening haze.
The Education Ministry has stipulated that all educational institutions under its purview in areas recording API readings above 180 must close from Oct 9.
Institutions in areas recording API readings above 150 for three consecutive days must also close from Oct 12.
4e469436c9f3f7ce: KUALA LUMPUR: BAM president Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz has welcomed the government's commitment to strengthening sports development under Budget 2027.

While no specific allocation for badminton was announced, he said the broader provisions for national sports development, school sports activities and high-performance competitions could create opportunities to strengthen the badminton talent pipeline.
BAM, whose annual expenditure is close to RM55 million, has been getting an allocation of RM5.5 million a year from the government for its programmes.

Budget 2027 allocates RM730 million for sports — RM460 million for national sports development and RM240 million to host the 2027 SEA Games and Asean Para Games, and RM30 million for the sports matching grant (GPS).

Tengku Zafrul said the 50 per cent increase in funding for school sports activities to RM27 million, which is expected to benefit more than 4.6 million students, was particularly encouraging as talent identification can begin at grassroots level.

"For badminton, talent development must begin at grassroots level. Therefore, the 50 per cent increase in the allocation for school sports activities to RM27 million, which will benefit more than 4.6 million students, is welcome," stated Tengku Zafrul on social media.

"However, development must not stop at school level. We must ensure talented players have a clear pathway to continue progressing through clubs, state associations and national development programmes."
Tengku Zafrul also welcomed the allocation under the GPS to encourage the organisation of high-performance sporting events.

He said BAM would examine how opportunities under Budget 2027, particularly through the GPS, could be leveraged with state associations and corporate partners to strengthen tournament organisation and provide greater exposure for emerging players.
Under the GPS, the government will reimburse 50 per cent of the organisational cost — up to a maximum of RM1 million — of an approved tournament.
"BAM also welcomes the GPS allocation to encourage the organisation of high-performance sporting events," added Tengku Zafrul.
"For badminton, more quality tournaments mean more opportunities for players to test their abilities, face stronger opponents and gain experience before competing on the international stage.
"Our goal is not merely to produce champions today, but to build a system capable of producing champions consistently for generations to come," he said.
8e7052a2c4c720c8: KUALA LUMPUR: Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (SKMM) memulakan siasatan terhadap seorang individu susulan kandungan disyaki menghina agama Islam, yang dimuat naik menerusi Facebook.

SKMM memaklumkan bahawa kandungan itu berkait penggunaan perkataan 'lighad', yang merujuk kepada ayat 18 Surah al-Hashr, dalam ucapan pembentangan Belanjawan 2027 oleh Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim semalam.
"Kandungan tersebut didakwa mempersenda ayat suci al-Quran, hingga menimbulkan kegusaran dalam kalangan masyarakat," menurut kenyataan.
SKMM memaklumkan pihaknya telah merakam percakapan individu berkenaan bagi membantu siasatan, serta menyita satu unit telefon bimbit dan e-sim untuk tujuan pemeriksaan forensik.

Kes disiasat mengikut Seksyen 233 Akta Komunikasi dan Multimedia, yang memperuntukkan hukuman denda maksimum RM500,000 atau penjara hingga dua tahun, atau kedua-duanya sekali, jika disabitkan kesalahan.
SKMM menegaskan kebebasan bersuara di media sosial perlu diamalkan secara bertanggungjawab dengan menghormati sensitiviti agama, serta memelihara keharmonian masyarakat berbilang kaum dan agama.

9a30e590e75307ce: BEIJING: French Open winner Mirra Andreeva will face Olympic champion and home favourite Zheng Qinwen in the China Open final after the Russian fourth seed eased past Nikola Bartunkova and unseeded Zheng overpowered Elise Mertens in Saturday's semi-finals.

Zheng, who received a wildcard entry to the tournament after recovering from an elbow injury, became the first Chinese player to reach the final in Beijing as she outplayed Belgian 13th seed Mertens 7-5 6-2 after Andreeva crushed Bartunkova 6-2 6-2.
Zheng made an early break to build a 4-2 lead, but made a number of errors to hand Mertens the break back.

But the 24-year-old, who is chasing her first WTA 1000 title on home soil, remained calm to build a 6-5 lead, before her strong crosscourt forehand earned her another break point which she converted when Mertens netted.
Zheng dominated the second set to secure her second clash with Andreeva, having beaten the Russian when they met in the 2024 Beijing quarter-finals.
Andreeva took an hour and 14 minutes to beat Bartunkova and reach her second WTA 1000 final of the year.
Czech Bartunkova committed 20 unforced errors, twice as many as Andreeva, as the world number five hit 27 winners to clinch victory.
"Just tried to play aggressive, I'm really happy with how I was playing. I really tried to be brave no matter what, and super happy with my performance today," Andreeva said.
b7d03a7243b9e891: PETALING JAYA: Schools and other educational institutions in Johor will remain closed for five more days from Monday due to the haze and deteriorating air quality across the state.
However, schools in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu will continue as usual tomorrow as air quality remains under control, the education ministry said.

The Johor decision to keep schools closed was announced by state executive councillor Dr Naqib Ghazali who said it was made at the order of the Johor regent, Tunku Ismail Sultan Ibrahim, to safeguard students’ health and safety.

“The state government believes that early preventive measures must receive priority, to reduce the risk of prolonged exposure to polluted air,” he said in a statement. Naqib said home-based teaching and learning would be implemented to ensure lessons could continue.
Unhealthy air pollution readings were recorded today in Pasir Gudang, Larkin, Tangkak, Segamat, Kota Tinggi, Pengerang, Batu Pahat and Kluang.

The education ministry said it would continue to monitor air quality. The ministry had previously directed school closures from Oct 9 in areas where air pollution readings exceeded 180, while those in areas with readings above 150 were to close from Oct 12.
e04e5e7b8c34c372: RAMALLAH, Palestinian Territories: Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections to September next year, official media said, confirming widespread speculation over the polls which were last held in 2006.
The vote will be held alongside presidential elections on Sept 11, 2027, Abbas said in a decree, blaming "obstacles" imposed by Israel, according to the Palestinian Wafa news agency.
The legislative elections, which the international community has strongly advocated for, had been scheduled for Nov 28 this year, while a presidential vote was expected in early 2027.
Israel had blasted Abbas's Palestinian Authority as "corrupt" over the anticipated delay.
"Abbas issued a presidential decree on Saturday calling for simultaneous presidential and legislative elections to be held on Sept 11, 2027," Abbas's office said in a statement published by Wafa.

The presidency blamed the delay on "obstacles imposed by Israeli measures that prevent elections from being held on their previously scheduled date, as well as the need to create appropriate political, security and on-the-ground conditions to ensure free, fair and inclusive elections."
This week, Abbas' Ramallah-based Palestinian Authority said Israel refused to allow Palestinian election officials access to east Jerusalem or Gaza ahead of the legislative elections.
Israel's foreign minister Gideon Saar on Friday had accused Abbas of "fooling the international community" by planning to postpone upcoming legislative polls.
Holding polls is part of the reforms demanded by the international community for the Palestinian Authority, including the European Union.
The last legislative elections in the Palestinian territories were held in 2006, when Islamist movement Hamas won. They defeated Fatah, which dominates the Palestinian Authority.
The ensuing rift set off a round of factional fighting, with Hamas later seizing power in the Gaza Strip and creating a territorial divide between Fatah in the West Bank and Hamas in Gaza.
As a result, the Palestinian Legislative Council, which is the PA's parliament, has not met since 2007.
Abbas won the last Palestinian presidential election in 2005, and his term should have expired in 2009, but he has since ruled by decree.
135581dc4772867b: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget was an effort by the government to ease the public's burdens through financial assistance, individual tax relief and tax reductions for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).

Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the approach included several measures to help the public cope with daily living expenses while easing the financial burden on workers and businesses.

Speaking after officiating the closing ceremony of the Johari Ghani Cup National Sports Day Futsal Carnival in Batu Caves, he said the measures also included financial assistance to help the public afford essential goods, with the amount of aid varying according to the recipient category.
"I noticed that in the budget announcement, the prime minister placed considerable emphasis on reducing the cost of living. There are various ways to address the cost of living.
"First, increasing financial assistance to help people purchase goods, supplementing their income with aid provided by the government.

"Second, providing some relief to salaried workers who have to pay taxes by allowing deductions and reducing their tax burden. Although the reductions may not be substantial, everyone can feel the benefits overall," he said.
edd8c286fc9c2f44: KUALA LUMPUR: Actor and television presenter Kamal Adli has described Indonesian actor Boy Hamzah's provocative remarks — sparked by a Malaysian boycott of an Indonesian personal care brand — as unprofessional and warned that such antics risk straining ties between the two neighbouring nations.
The 40-year-old artiste stressed that the controversy should not be blown out of proportion to the point of inciting hostility or leading either side to belittle the other country.
Instead, he urged all parties to show maturity when handling differing viewpoints and to refrain from entertaining statements that could escalate tension.

"I think he was being unprofessional. I know he was actually triggered. But we don't need to get worked up or retaliate. We should just focus on taking care of our families and children rather than giving weight to these issues," Kamal said.
"I don't know who he is, but if you look at Malaysia, which local artiste or celebrity goes around bashing another country? None of us does that.

"There's no need to meddle in such matters. It started with football and then moved on to a brand. There's really no reason to go so far as to put down another nation," he added when met during the recent press conference and launch of the Anugerah Melodi Terhangat (AMT) 2026 X Cuckootopia at the Hyatt Regency Kuala Lumpur.
Elaborating further, Kamal noted that public statements must be weighed carefully to prevent situations from deteriorating.
He maintained that rivalries or disagreements stemming from football should end once the match is over, rather than being dragged out to trigger larger disputes.
"Whatever he says is heard by the public, and it can make things worse. Originally, it was just about football. Once it's over, let it be. We shouldn't keep carrying it forward," he remarked.
Kamal appealed to Malaysians to stop commenting on or feeding into the provocation so that friction between the two countries does not escalate further.
He noted that Malaysians have already made their stance clear, adding that there is no need to prolong the feud to the extent of insulting leaders or citizens of the neighbouring country.
"As Malaysians, we have already voiced what needed to be said. So, I feel we should stop here. Let them shadowbox on their own. Enough is enough. We are above this level," he said.

"We don't need to resort to insulting their leaders or people. Many of us are friends with Indonesians living here, and some of us work together. To our netizens, enough is enough — don't entertain it. It's better to focus on the worsening haze situation right now."
Earlier, Boy Hamzah had shared a video on social media commenting on the Malaysian boycott of the Indonesian brand.
In the clip, the Indonesian actor pointed out his country's vastly larger population compared to Malaysia's, claiming the local boycott would have little to no impact on the brand.
He also waded into historical claims, asserting that Malaysia would not exist without Indonesia, which quickly ignited outrage online.
ad18af9471855e52: MELAKA: The public have been advised against sharing social media content that insults, provokes or incites hostility over religion, race and the royal institution (3R), and instead to report such content to the authorities for further action.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said resharing such content would only widen its reach, including by increasing its view count on social media.
"Do not help spread it, do not reshare it, do not give it views. File a police report or lodge a complaint with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).

"Both responsible agencies will take immediate action," he told reporters after officiating at the Madani Kita Programme (PMK) 2026 with the Paya Rumput@Tangga Batu community at the Krubong People's Housing Project (PPR) here today.

Fahmi was responding to a social media post by influencer Lim Sian See, whose real name is Datuk Eric Se-To, questioning the use of the word "lighad" in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's speech when tabling the Supply Bill (Budget 2027) in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
In the post, Lim questioned the word before making a sarcastic association with another word.
The word "lighad", which appears in verse 18 of Surah al-Hasyr, refers to tomorrow or the future.

Fahmi said police and MCMC were tracing the individual to assist in investigations and have a statement recorded, adding that any further action would depend on the findings and the prosecution's consideration.

"We have identified the individual who insulted Islam yesterday by ridiculing the word 'lighad'. I understand that several police reports have been lodged ... at least one of those reports has been brought to my attention," he said.
43f00afaa2881c38: PETALING JAYA: Semua sekolah dan institusi pendidikan di Johor ditutup selama lima hari lagi kerana jerebu dan kemerosotan kualiti udara.

Kerajaan Johor mengumumkan tempoh penutupan sekolah dan institusi pendidikan dilanjutkan bermula 12 Okt hingga 16 Okt setelah meneliti perkembangan semasa pencemaran udara, serta risiko gangguan pernafasan dalam kalangan kanak-kanak dan warga pendidikan.

"Keputusan pelanjutan tempoh penutupan ini dibuat dengan mengambil kira beberapa faktor utama berdasarkan penilaian situasi semasa," kata Exco Pendidikan dan Penerangan Johor, Naqib Ghazali, dalam kenyataan.
Selain risiko kesihatan, kerajaan negeri mengambil kira bacaan Indeks Pencemar Udara (IPU) yang dilaporkan berada sekitar 170 hingga 180 tanpa menunjukkan perubahan ketara.

Kerajaan negeri juga mengambil kira pergerakan udara yang perlahan serta keadaan atmosfera yang kurang membantu penyebaran bahan pencemar, sekali gus berpotensi menyebabkan jerebu berlarutan untuk tempoh yang lebih panjang.
Turut diambil kira jangkaan pergerakan angin dari arah Kalimantan, Indonesia bagi tempoh 13 Okt hingga 15 Okt yang berpotensi membawa pencemaran udara rentas sempadan.
"Kerajaan negeri berpandangan bahawa langkah pencegahan awal perlu diberikan keutamaan bagi mengurangkan risiko pendedahan berpanjangan kepada udara tercemar," katanya.
"Keputusan ini turut memgambil kira keperluan memastikan persekitaran pembelajaran yang selamat dan kondusif sebelum sesi persekolahan secara bersemuka dapat diteruskan."

Kerajaan negeri menggesa ibu bapa dan penjaga mengehadkan aktiviti luar anak-anak, memastikan mereka minum air secukupnya serta mendapatkan pemeriksaan dan rawatan segera jika mengalami gejala seperti batuk berpanjangan, sakit tekak atau kesukaran bernafas.
Orang ramai juga diminta mematuhi nasihat kesihatan pihak berkuasa dan mendapatkan maklumat terkini melalui saluran rasmi.
Pada 7 Oktober lalu, Johor mengumumkan penutupan sekolah selama dua hari bermula keesokan hari susulan keadaan jerebu serta kemerosotan kualiti udara.
Penutupan itu dibuat atas titah Pemangku Sultan Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail sebagai langkah melindungi keselamatan dan kesihatan murid.

36317ca0022aa4f3: SHANGHAI: A moustached Carlos Alcaraz beat Juan Manuel Cerundolo 6-3, 6-3 to kick-start his title bid at the Shanghai Masters on Saturday, days after winning the Tokyo Open for his first trophy since returning from injury.
The Spanish star, seeded second, put on a dominant show to brush aside the 55th-ranked Argentinian in the second round in just 66 minutes.
"Really, really happy with the way I played today. It wasn't easy," said the 23-year-old former number one.
"Just had two days of preparation... I came from Tokyo, there were totally different conditions," he added. "Just tried to play the best that I can."
Sporting a fresh moustache, Alcaraz signed a camera "Moustache Team" following his win.
Asked by an on-court interviewer about the new look, Alcaraz said: "It's gonna stay."
He will play either Ignacio Buse or Zizou Bergs in the next round.

Medvedev was defaulted from his semi-final against Novak Djokovic in Beijing for hitting a spectator with a ball and ended the 500-level event with zero ranking points and no prize money.
The former world number one said it was an accident.
Playing five days later in Shanghai, sixth-ranked Medvedev overcame an early wobble to hold off 59th-ranked Struff.
He sent down 21 aces to advance and will face Czech qualifier Dalibor Svrcina in the next round.
World number five Felix Auger-Aliassime also survived a scare, needing three hours to beat 77th-ranked Camilo Ugo Carabelli 4-6, 7-6 (7/1), 7-5.
The Canadian will play Spaniard Pablo Carreno Busta in the third round.
Several matches in the afternoon were suspended due to rain, but Taylor Fritz, Casper Ruud and Arthur Fils all went through as play resumed.

6a7dbf47781e02de: The sports-mad city has embraced its new superstar, even as he choppers in from Manhattan and makes no secret of the fact that Philly was never his first choice Philadelphia has always had an instinctive affinity with athletes who embrace the grind over the glamour. In a place where sports mean a little too much, commitment has traditionally counted for more than celebrity. 4b710218b4d27f97: COLOGNE, Oct 10 — French astronaut Sophie Adenot went through “all human emotions, from the most joyful to the hardest” during her eight months in space, she said back on solid ground today in Germany.

Adenot splashed down in the Pacific Ocean Thursday off the coast of California in the Dragon capsule that carried Crew-12, having returned to Earth from a mission on the International Space Station (ISS).
She had spent a total of 235 days in space, breaking the record for the longest uninterrupted orbital stay by a European astronaut.

At 400km away from Earth, Adenot could see there are “no divisions, no borders” but “just a precious planet that we all share,” she said today on the tarmac of the European Space Agency (ESA) training centre in Cologne, occasionally in tears.
The 44-year-old astronaut looked visibly weakened on her arrival in Germany and was assisted by two ESA physicians.
In space, the body adapts to the absence of gravity, which leads to bone loss, muscle wasting, cardiovascular deconditioning and even visual problems.
Adenot must now begin an intensive recovery program of about three weeks to regain her pre-flight condition.
“It’s a cocktail of astonishing emotions, it’s incredible. It’s great to be back on Earth, but it also comes with its share of challenges, especially physiological ones,” she told a press conference.
She also described the “difficult” moment of Thursday’s splashdown, when the capsule bringing back the four astronauts on her team had to endure “a lot of waves for 25 minutes”.
“And when the commandos pulled me out of the capsule, the first thing I said to them was, ‘Send me back to space, please!’ It was much easier up there,” she added.

During the mission, Adenot became the first French female astronaut to venture outside the space station for a spacewalk. In all, she undertook three spacewalks on August 18 and 25, and September 1. — AFP
e5d58bfc5e4dee80: JERUSALEM, Oct 10 — One year after US President Donald Trump declared the war in Gaza to be over, few of the long-term promises of the ceasefire have come to fruition.
Here is a list of some of the key points of the October 10, 2025 ceasefire and where things stand:
Hostages released, calm in Israel
Three days after the agreement was announced, Hamas freed the 20 remaining living hostages seized during the group’s October 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest day in Israel’s history.
The captives’ return was a key priority for Israel, whose public had agonised over their fate.
The ceasefire anniversary also marks one year of quiet for Israel from the Gaza front, with no rocket attacks by Hamas.
The group’s missile inventory was depleted by near-constant Israeli bombardment, which damaged or destroyed the vast majority of buildings in the Palestinian territory.
The US military set up a command post with foreign allies near the Gaza border to monitor the truce.
No Israeli withdrawal or let-up
Israel has reduced its level of attacks but has kept striking Gaza on a near-daily basis.

Israeli strikes have killed some 1,450 Palestinians since the ceasefire, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas and whose figures are considered accurate by the United Nations.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is in a tight election race, has vowed to kill everyone involved in the October 7 attack.
Netanyahu said on the attack’s anniversary that 4,000 out of 6,000 “Hamas monsters” had been killed.
Israeli forces were allowed to stay in 53 per cent of Gaza under the terms of the ceasefire, but a year later they control about 70 per cent of it, according to official accounts.
Hamas remains, with weapons

The second phase of the agreement was supposed to include a political transition away from Hamas, and technocrat Ali Shaath was appointed head of a new National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG).
Hamas announced in July that it was disbanding its governing body and handing over Gaza’s administration to the US-blessed NCAG.
But Hamas effectively remains in charge of security in Gaza, and Shaath has taken a low profile.
The Palestinian Islamist movement elected a new leader, Khalil al-Hayya, in July. Shortly afterwards, the group announced it would give up its weapons, a step hailed by Trump as a breakthrough.
But Israel has been sceptical, with Netanyahu demanding verifiable decommissioning of all weapons down to individual guns.
Hamas has not gone ahead with disarmament, and Israel has refused to reciprocate by starting to withdraw forces.
Reconstruction just talk

Trump set up a new global body for the deal dubbed the “Board of Peace”, tapping as key figures former British prime minister Tony Blair and Bulgarian diplomat Nickolay Mladenov, who serves as “Gaza high representative”.

Trump, a critic of foreign aid, in January promised US$10 billion (RM41 billion) in US funding to the board he controls, and Gulf allies have pledged more, but no money is known to have made its way to Gaza reconstruction.
In September, the board proposed a US$2.45 billion Gaza recovery plan at a meeting of its members and stakeholders, in an effort meant to span over six months. — AFP
80368939c975f5a4: KHAN YUNIS, Oct 10 — Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a community kitchen in the hope of getting some food for her family.
It has been a year since a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel was supposed to allow food to flood into the ruined territory, yet widespread hunger persists there.
Masri has little choice. Without the kitchen run by humanitarian groups, she and her eight children would have “nothing at all”, the 35-year-old told AFP.
Each day she sets out early in the morning and returns in the afternoon, this time bringing four containers of rice, lentils and a little chicken, which the family throws itself at.
Among them is her husband, wounded in both legs by an airstrike, meaning he “cannot go and fight with the others” to get food.
This will be the only meal of the day for the family of 10, living in a tent in Khan Yunis. There was no breakfast and they will have no dinner.
What little flour they have, Masri explained, has to be rationed.
In August 2025, a United Nations-backed body, the IPC, declared a state of famine in Gaza, though Israel quickly denounced it as a lie.
By December, the UN had lifted that declaration, saying that the ceasefire had allowed in enough supplies over the course of two months to ease conditions.
COGAT, the Israeli defence ministry organisation responsible for civilian affairs in the Palestinian territories, told AFP that the humanitarian situation in Gaza was stable.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Morsi and Nihaya Al-Masri, a displaced Palestinian couple from Beit Hanoun, are seen at their makeshift shelter in Khan Yunis, in the southern Gaza Strip, October 6, 2026. — AFP pic
But Shaun Hughes, of the UN’s World Food Programme, was less sanguine.
The food security situation, he said, “is still extremely serious”.
The most recent figures, from July, show that “1.4 million out of the population of about 2.1 million people are acutely food insecure”, he said, with 200,000 of them “just one step below famine”.
‘Shameful’
While some food is getting in, a lack of sufficient nutritional variety continues to pose a health threat.
“Dietary diversity is a major food security issue in Gaza,” said Hughes.

“You cannot survive on dry goods and wheat flour and bread alone. Particularly children, particularly pregnant and breastfeeding mothers, they need the micronutrients that come with high protein foods, fresh vegetables, fresh fruits,” he explained.
Masri said that her children, aged between three and 14, “dream of eating fruit” but the family doesn’t have the means to buy any.
She said one of her sons suffered from malnutrition during the 2025 famine, although “little by little, his condition is improving”.
Malnutrition isn’t only caused by a lack of food, but also essential nutrients. It weakens the immune system of children, making them vulnerable to illnesses and stunting their growth.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

The children of Nihaya Al-Masri, a 35-year-old displaced Palestinian woman from Beit Hanoun, sharing a meal provided by a charity kitchen in Khan Yunis, in the southern Gaza Strip, October 6, 2026. — AFP pic
“Repeated bouts of acute malnutrition amongst children is something that human beings just don’t recover from,” said Hughes.
Cognitive and physical impairments “continue into later life”, he added.

At Khan Yunis’s Nasser hospital, the head of the malnutrition unit, Israa al-Najjar, told AFP she had “observed an increase in syndromes and conditions” linked to malnutrition that affect the immune system.

In a report published on Thursday, the day after the third anniversary of the October 7 Hamas attack that sparked the Gaza war, Medecins du Monde published a study that found 93 per cent of pregnant or breastfeeding women had symptoms of anaemia, which is closely linked to malnutrition.
Just 17 per cent had a sufficiently varied diet to meet their nutritional needs, the group found.
All the while, Masri has kept visiting the community kitchen, despite asthma leaving her exhausted.
Her children spend their days collecting “pieces of nylon, bits of cardboard and chunks of foam” to try and reinforce their tent, which is in a poor state.
She said it was “shameful” that her children had to do so.
“I swear to God, this isn’t normal.” — AFP
80b0658afb596507: NIR AM, Oct 10 — Like hundreds of thousands of Israelis, Amihai will be of voting age for the first time since Hamas carried out its attack on October 7, 2023. When he casts his ballot this month, he has one priority above all — security.

From a field overlooking the sprawling ruins of the northern Gaza Strip, the 18-year-old says he plans to vote for a far-right party at the ballot box, three years after the deadliest day in Israeli history.
“I’m voting based solely on security — not for whoever will help me buy an apartment in 10 years, but for whoever can guarantee that I’ll even still be alive here in 10 years,” he told AFP.
Amihai, from Shomria in southern Israel, was speaking less than two kilometres from Gaza, swathes of which have been flattened by Israeli bombardment since the war with Hamas erupted in 2023.

He was attending an event calling for Jewish settlement of the Palestinian territory, and said that on October 27 he would be casting a vote for the ultra-nationalist party of National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir.

“After October 7, I want death for the terrorists, I want the terrorists here to suffer in prison, I want there to be deterrence,” the teenager said, alluding to a recently passed death penalty law that applies to Palestinians.

Sporting a cap and T-shirt in support of the minister, Amihai said he also wanted “emigration from Gaza, that the people of Gaza will be dying to leave” — another policy advocated by government ministers in recent months.
Roughly 550,000 Israelis aged between 18 and 22 will be voting for the first time in October, according to Israel’s Channel 12.

In a recent poll commissioned by the channel, 74 per cent of first-time voters described their policy views as right or centre-right — an even higher share than the broadly right-leaning public at large.
‘Real future’
The trend stands in contrast to many Western democracies where young people are among the most left-leaning voters — with some in recent years motivated by outrage over Israel’s actions in Gaza.
But the right-wing turn of Israeli Jewish youth has been building for around two decades, said pollster and analyst Dahlia Scheindlin.
“Older people... remember the hope of reaching full, comprehensive peace agreements with the Palestinians,” Scheindlin told AFP.
“Anybody who’s an 18-year-old now, his or her entire political consciousness is under (Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu, it’s a very ultra-nationalist environment,” she said.
“Peace is not in people’s minds.”
At a gathering of young activists for the centre-left Democrats party in Tel Aviv last month, 18-year-old Gili said she felt society had turned its back on peace.

“I think especially young people, when they see something so huge happening, something that hurts so deeply and affects everyone, like what happened on October 7, then the first tendency is fear, to be afraid, and not to believe that peace is possible,” she told AFP.
“It’s really logical that everyone kind of became more and more right-wing, and more and more extreme.”
Hamas’s October 7 attack resulted in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.

In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive that has killed more than 74,200 people in Gaza, according to the health ministry there, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
Gili and her friends at the rally said they supported the Democrats’ vision of a political agreement with the Palestinians.
“Conflict management is not a solution, and I don’t think the current situation can go on,” said Yuval, an 18-year-old from kibbutz Tel Yitzhak in central Israel.
“Certainly not if we want to raise our children here, if we want to believe we have a real future for ourselves”.
‘Win decisively’

For yeshiva student Yishai Neeman, who hopes soon to enlist in a combat unit in the Israeli military, the horrors of October 7 and the wars that followed strengthened his resolve to fight for his country.
Neeman, who is now 19, was at a synagogue when he heard of Hamas’s attack and spent his final years at boarding school running to bomb shelters.
From his home in the central city of Petah Tikva, Neeman said he would be voting for the Religious Zionism party of far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich.
Neeman said he wanted peace, but felt it wasn’t possible under the current conditions. Israel should annex the occupied West Bank, he said, and “erase their hope for a Palestinian state”.
Soon heading to fight himself, Neeman said he wasn’t in favour of endless wars, but that Israel “can’t return once more to the understanding that preceded October 7”.
“That’s why now we must fight and win decisively.” — AFP

a713347ad27a9cc0: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Oil blending activities must obtain written approval from the Customs director-general where required under the relevant regulations, and be backed by complete documentation to ensure legal compliance and transparent transactions, an expert said.

Maritime, Customs and cross-border trade policy and law expert Madzli Harun said every activity involving the import, storage, blending and re-export of oil must be carried out within the scope of the licence and the conditions set by the authorities.

He said blending could alter a product’s composition and specifications, so clear records were needed to verify quantities, cargo movements and the condition of the product before and after the process.
Related documents such as contracts, bills of lading and cargo manifests must be aligned to ensure the information declared matched the actual transactions and the condition of the goods, he said.

“If a premises is only approved for storage, any additional activities such as blending or changing a product’s grade must be scrutinised based on the scope of the licence and the regulations in force.

“Operators must ensure written approval is obtained when required, and that all activities are recorded accurately,” he said at a forum titled “Strengthening Malaysia’s Downstream Petroleum Value Chain and Identifying Gaps and Enabling Factors Within Malaysia’s Regulatory Landscape”, organised by Maritime Network Sdn Bhd in collaboration with Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT).

Madzli said incomplete documentation, or discrepancies between records and the actual condition of the cargo, could raise questions over the declaration of goods, regulatory compliance and tax treatment.
A thorough audit was also important to ensure the volumes of oil received, stored, blended and exported could be identified and matched against the relevant documents, he added.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said responsible petroleum cargo management was not merely an operational matter, but also a question of protecting the country’s interests and ensuring future generations inherited a maritime industry built on transparency, safety and accountability.

In cross-border trade, he said, determining the origin of goods and their eligibility for treatment under free trade agreements must be based on the rules of origin and the relevant supporting documents.

As such, industry operators must ensure every transaction complied with the set conditions, while the authorities must have sufficient records to assess compliance levels and tax implications, he said.

He said clear controls over blending, including approval requirements and proper documentation, were key to preserving the integrity of the Customs system and reducing the risk of disputes between industry players and the authorities.

Meanwhile, maritime industry expert Nazery Khalid said oil blending carried out without approval, monitoring, compliance with standards and proper documentation must be taken seriously, as incidents could threaten health and safety and undermine the integrity of the authorities responsible for monitoring such activities.
He said if such incidents occurred, questions would arise over compliance with safety procedures, the effectiveness of monitoring and the enforcement of regulations on oil blending.

Approval, documentation oversight and compliance with operating conditions must be given close attention to ensure every activity was carried out in a controlled manner, in line with the set regulations as well as international standards and best practices, he said.

He said weaknesses and a lack of integrity in documentation, supervision and enforcement could not only pose risks to the public and the environment, but also erode the confidence of industry players, trading partners and the international community in the transparency of Malaysia’s cargo-handling regulatory system.

“Inconsistent and inaccurate cargo documents such as the bill of lading and manifest should not be taken lightly, especially for liquid cargo such as petroleum products and palm oil. They could open the door to various forms of misconduct that could harm health and the environment.

“If this situation is not addressed promptly and comprehensively, it could undermine public confidence in the integrity of the industry concerned and damage the country’s image on the international stage,” he said.

At the end of the session, Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said responsible petroleum cargo management was not merely an operational matter, but also a question of protecting the country’s interests and ensuring future generations inherited a maritime industry built on transparency, safety and accountability.

9a42f3045e49f3c2: PETALING JAYA: Celebrity chef Redzuawan Ismail, better known as Chef Wan, said his great-grandfather was a Kuching pioneer and prominent merchant Ong Tiang Swee.
Chef Wan made the revelation in a series of Instagram posts during a visit to the Chinese History Museum in Sarawak’s capital.
“Just imagine, this is my great-grandfather, Ong Tiang Swee. These are all the pioneers and community leaders,” he said, adding that Ong was his maternal grandmother’s father.
Chef Wan said his great-grandfather, who has a road named after him in the capital, died in Kuching in 1950 and was accorded a state funeral.
He said Ong was one of two Chinese people nominated to the Sarawak legislative council in 1937.
Chef Wan said his great-grandfather’s wealth was seized and the family “lost everything” during the Japanese invasion. He said his great-grandmother was sent back to Singapore with his mother.
029153cac7a3b7bf: SEREMBAN, Oct 10 — The provision of better infrastructure facilities is expected to enhance Negeri Sembilan’s attractiveness as an investment destination, in line with the ongoing development of Malaysia Vision Valley 2.0 (MVV 2.0).

Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the construction of a new road from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to Bandar Enstek was among the key infrastructure facilities that would support development in the area, while facilitating movement and improving accessibility.

“Alhamdulillah, Negeri Sembilan is not being left behind in benefiting from Budget 2027 announced yesterday. Among the initiatives are a new road from KLIA to Bandar Enstek, as well as the upgrading of Jalan Pajam-Nilai-Salak. The new road will also complement the development of MVV 2.0.

“This is significant and a good selling point for the state government, while giving Negeri Sembilan an advantage in attracting more investors,” he told reporters after the close of the Negeri Sembilan Malaysia Property Expo (Mapex) today, which was also attended by state Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda) chairman Datuk Hoo Kim See.

Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027, said the Madani government would complete the development of MVV 2.0 with infrastructure projects including the new KLIA-Bandar Enstek road, the upgrading of Jalan Pajam-Nilai-Salak and the implementation of the Klang Valley Dual Track 2 project.

Meanwhile, Ismail said the construction of the Rembau Integrated Health Complex would also benefit the state by expanding healthcare facilities for the public, particularly as several existing hospitals in Negeri Sembilan were facing problems, including a shortage of beds.

He said the facility was important to increase the state’s healthcare service capacity and complement the government’s efforts to improve healthcare facilities to meet the needs of a growing population.
He also expressed hope that initiatives announced under Budget 2027 would be implemented according to schedule to ensure the people could enjoy the intended benefits as planned.

Ismail said smooth implementation within the stipulated timeframe was crucial, as delays or problems with project execution could prompt complaints from the public, who had high expectations following the government’s announcements.

“What matters is not just the announcement of expenditure, but also how it is implemented. Sometimes, we announce a lot, but implementation gets held up and does not proceed on time. This will create problems for the people who have placed their hopes in these announcements,” he said.

He said the state government would continue to facilitate and cooperate through the relevant departments to ensure the projects could be implemented smoothly, allowing the people to benefit within the stipulated timeframe. — Bernama

4fa51f4bdf777393: PUTRAJAYA: Belanjawan 2027 memberi penekanan kepada pembangunan sosial, kesejahteraan masyarakat serta usaha memperkukuh perpaduan dan keharmonian dalam kalangan rakyat Malaysia, kata Menteri Perpaduan Negara Aaron Ago Dagang.

"Melalui belanjawan, Kementerian Perpaduan Negara menerima peruntukan sebanyak RM858,794,400 iaitu RM793,039,400 bagi perbelanjaan mengurus dan RM65,755,000 bagi perbelanjaan pembangunan.

"Peruntukan ini meningkat sebanyak 11.82% berbanding 2026, sekali gus mencerminkan keutamaan kerajaan dalam memperkukuh agenda perpaduan, keharmonian masyarakat dan pembinaan negara bangsa," menurut kenyataan.

Belanjawan itu turut memperlihatkan komitmen berterusan kerajaan dalam memastikan pembangunan negara dilaksanakan secara seimbang, dengan mengambil kira pertumbuhan ekonomi, kesejahteraan rakyat serta pengukuhan tatakelola.
Beliau berkata Belanjawan 2027 turut menyediakan peruntukan bagi pelaksanaan pelbagai inisiatif dan pembangunan yang memberi tumpuan kepada pengukuhan perpaduan dan keharmonian masyarakat.
Semalam, Anwar membentangkan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat yang memperuntukkan RM510 bilion bagi mengangkat martabat dan kesejahteraan rakyat pada semua peringkat.
5ce30406f64c9860: PETALING JAYA: Perlis dan Wilayah Tashkent di Uzbekistan sedang meneroka peluang memperluas kerjasama dalam sektor pertanian dan pelancongan, termasuk potensi pembangunan tanaman kenaf di wilayah itu.
Gabenor Wilayah Tashkent Zoyir Mirzayev berkata, kerjasama itu boleh diperkukuh menerusi perkongsian kepakaran serta pemanfaatan sumber ekonomi dan kelebihan yang dimiliki kedua-dua pihak.

"Usaha itu mencerminkan perkembangan positif perbincangan terdahulu dalam mengenal pasti bidang pertanian yang berpotensi dikembangkan melalui kerjasama strategik," menurut kenyataan mengenai pertemuan itu.
Dalam sektor pelancongan, kedua-dua pihak turut membincangkan peluang kerjasama dengan memanfaatkan tarikan dan keunikan destinasi masing-masing bagi merancakkan kegiatan ekonomi.

Perkara itu dibangkitkan Zoyir pada majlis santapan malam yang dihoskannya bagi meraikan Raja Muda Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail dan Raja Puan Muda Perlis Tuanku Lailatul Shahreen Akashah Khalil.
Majlis berkenaan berlangsung di Amirsoy Mountain Resort, sebuah pusat peranginan pergunungan kira-kira 80km dari bandar Tashkent, sebelum pasangan diraja itu berangkat pulang ke tanah air.

Zoyir turut menyifatkan hubungan baiknya dengan Raja Perlis Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Jamalullail serta Tuanku Syed Faizuddin sebagai 'asas penting untuk terus memperkukuh hubungan dan kerjasama antara kedua-dua pihak'.
Turut hadir, Duta Besar Malaysia ke Uzbekistan Rafeedah Abdul Aziz dan Mufti Perlis Mohd Asri Zainul Abidin.
Anakanda puteri kedua pasangan diraja itu, Sharifah Farah Adriana Jamalullail turut berangkat ke majlis berkenaan.
Pada April tahun lalu, Zoyir mengadakan lawatan kerja ke Perlis dan menghadap Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin di Istana Arau, selain mengunjungi Universiti Malaysia Perlis.
Beliau turut menyertai program Kayuhan Amal MAIPs Peduli di kawasan Projek Transformasi Diraja Kampung Nelayan Warna-Warni Seberang Ramai, Kuala Perlis.
Susulan lawatan itu, Zoyir yang diiringi Duta Besar Uzbekistan ke Malaysia Karomiddin Gadoev memilih Perlis secara rasmi sebagai rakan kerjasama utama Wilayah Tashkent di Malaysia.
